analysis.title: Hedging The AI Bust: Goldman FICC Says Look To Tokyo As France Goes "Orbital"
key_insights: Goldman prime brokerage data as of Oct 19 showed the largest two-week net selling of Global Info Tech in the 10+ year history of the series (-3.3 standard deviations), with short leverage at the 99th percentile on a five-year lookback.

Credit of lower-rated borrowers has been the 'eye of the storm' in the AI selloff, as markets reassess AI buildout economics under potentially higher-for-longer long-term rates and energy cost pressures.
Goldman credit strategists are underweight USD IG Tech and neutral HY, expecting AI-related issuer dispersion to remain high, particularly in project finance bonds.

USD project finance issuance hit roughly $105 billion in 2026 YTD (as of Oct 13), almost all data centers and chip/compute financing. That is about 4x the previous record (2020, roughly $25 billion across all sectors) and nearly triple 2025.
Bernstein sees a $76 billion funding hole at CoreWeave.

Middle East escalation risk sent Brent to fresh local highs after reports of US and Israeli plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the elections, US diplomat departures from Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes, and Aramco evacuation orders for its Dhahran headquarters.

Goldman's commodity team base case (2027 Gulf supply 0.3mb/d below Feb '26) has Brent sliding toward the mid-$70s by late 2027, below the forward curve. The upside case (2027 Gulf supply 5mb/d below pre-war levels) sends Brent to roughly $140+ by early 2027.

USD rates remain better bid despite oil risk. Goldman's Chryssafis reads the market as treating the NYT report as unconfirmed while the AI de-rating looks more sustained. Real yields are 'in the driving seat'.
The 10Y Treasury yield sits at about 5.00% with the 10Y real yield at 2.67%, both off late-September peaks but far above year-start levels.

French 10Y OAT/Bund spread reached 173bps (from 159bps on Oct 2, the widest since 2011), with French 10Y yields at 5.08%. The spread is the widest since the euro's introduction and absolute yield is above Eurozone crisis levels.
Goldman strategists see energy price relief as the clearest route to French spread compression. Without it they expect wider spreads and more pressure on EUR FX.

The 5Y EUR-USD real rate differential has fallen to -136bps, roughly where it was in early 2025 when EURUSD traded near 1.03, while EURUSD is still at 1.12. The desk has seen demand for EURUSD downside.
Goldman's desk sees interest in USDJPY put overlay hedges against an AI bust. GSDEER has the yen roughly 40% undervalued vs the dollar, the cheapest currency on its list.
Goldman's logic: if AI concerns spiral into US-unexceptionalism and US-Japan rate differentials compress, sustained repatriation from US assets back to Japan would mean USD selling and JPY buying.

Supporting factors for a stronger yen: Japanese officials' interest in a strong JPY, PM Takaichi's push for domestic investment, and signs the BoJ will keep hiking gradually (Japan's biggest labor group seeks a midpoint 6% target in 2027 wage talks, per Reuters).
2Y USDJPY ATM implied vol is 9.9, versus a 20-year average of 13.8 and a 20-year low of 8.4.

Since Oct 14 (when Goldman's AI Leaders basket fell 4.7%), the basket's correlation with the S&P 500 rose from 0.73 to 0.91, with 10Y yield changes flipped from -0.13 to +0.19, and with USDJPY swung from -0.34 to +0.46. AI down now means S&P down, yields down and yen up.
Goldman continues to like equities-down / yields-down dual binaries as growth shock hedges. The scenario that breaks them is the $140 Brent tail, where yields rise with oil and stocks fall anyway.

trade_ideas.description: Buy USDJPY puts (2Y ATM implied vol 9.9) as an overlay hedge against an AI de-rating
trade_ideas.rationale: AI-driven US-unexceptionalism would compress US-Japan rate differentials and trigger repatriation into Japan, with the yen about 40% undervalued per GSDEER and implied vol near 20-year lows.

trade_ideas.description: Equities down / yields down dual binaries as growth shock hedges
trade_ideas.rationale: Realized correlations have flipped back to AI down, 10Y yields lower and USD softer vs JPY.
trade_ideas.risk: A $140 Brent tail where yields rise with oil and stocks fall anyway would break the dual binary.

trade_ideas.rationale: The 5Y real rate differential at -136bps points to EURUSD near 1.03, versus 1.12 spot, giving a valuation cushion for hedges, with vol still low.

risk_factors: Escalation in the Middle East, including a Gulf supply shock sending Brent to $140+.
AI de-rating spreading from equities to credit, especially project finance bonds tied to data centers.
CoreWeave funding gap of $76 billion (Bernstein) and distress among junk issuers tied to AI.
French bond stress and fragmentation risk in Europe, with Italy trading 50bps inside France.
Higher-for-longer long-term rates and energy cost pressures raising the cost of capital for the AI buildout.
Record hedge fund shorting could produce short-covering bounces.

2Y USDJPY ATM implied vol at 9.9 vs 20-year average of 13.8 and 20-year low of 8.4, making USDJPY put protection cheap.

geopolitical: US and Israel reportedly drawing up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the elections (NYT, unconfirmed).
US ordered diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes (Reuters).
Saudi Aramco told staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters, which suffered extensive damage in a Houthi attack the prior week.
Rising frequency of attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in October. Trump accused Iran of making up fake attacks to drive up oil prices.
French political and fiscal stress as lawmakers grapple with debt while protestors riot over the cost of living.
Japanese policy: officials' interest in a strong JPY and PM Takaichi's push for domestic investment in local financial assets.
cross_bank_references: Bernstein now sees a $76 billion funding hole at CoreWeave.
Nomura's Charlie McElligott says bonds are 'working as your hedge' again.
Goldman's delta-one desk piece 'The Reflexivity Is Striking' carries the same message on the AI scare outlasting the oil scare.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil and Gulf escalation drive inflation risk and could keep yields rising, with the NYT report on Iran strikes possibly denied by the administration.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI de-rating is more sustained (credit stress in neoclouds/hyperscalers, equity weakness in semis), so bonds rally on growth fears, with the S&P now 0.91-correlated to an AI basket.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A $140 Brent tail where yields rise with oil and stocks fall anyway breaks the equities-down / yields-down dual binary.
